title: Software Engineer I (New Grad) - Consumer Experience
location: New York, New York, United States
description:
StubHub is on a mission to redefine the live event experience on a global scale. Whether someone is looking to attend their first event or their hundredth, we’re here to delight them all the way from the moment they start looking for a ticket until they step through the gate. The same goes for our sellers. From fans selling a single ticket to the promoters of a worldwide stadium tour, we want StubHub to be the safest, most convenient way to offer a ticket to the millions of fans who browse our platform around the world.
 StubHub is on a mission to redefine the live event experience on a global scale. Whether someone is looking to attend their first event or their hundredth, we’re here to delight them—from the moment they start searching for tickets to the moment they’re walking into the venue.
 At StubHub, we’re not just selling tickets; we’re elevating the entire live event experience. Fans come to us to discover, buy, and sell tickets to the events they love—and our engineers make that experience fast, intuitive, and trustworthy across web and mobile.
 This role is designed for new graduates who want hands-on production experience, strong mentorship, and exposure to modern engineering practices, including AI-assisted development and GenAI tools in a collaborative team environment. You’ll work closely with Senior Engineers and SDE IIs, shipping meaningful features while leveling up quickly.
 Location: Hybrid (3 days in office / 2 days remote) — New York, NY
 About the Team:  
 The Consumer Experience team owns the end-to-end journey for millions of fans discovering, buying, and selling tickets on StubHub’s web and mobile platforms. Every search, recommendation, checkout flow, and confirmation page is built by our teams.
 We operate at global scale, serving fans across 60+ regions and 30+ languages with fast, localized, and reliable experiences during high-demand moments. This is high-impact engineering with real-time traffic spikes and complex distributed systems challenges.
 Our teams are deeply cross-functional, with engineering, product, design, and data working in true partnership and shared ownership. Engineers influence strategy, shape roadmaps, and have direct access to experimentation and insights that guide decisions.
 We build across the full stack, choosing tools and technologies that help us move quickly and deliver quality at scale. We are relentless about understanding fans, using data and rapid iteration to raise the bar on every release.
 If you are excited to build products used by millions, solve meaningful technical challenges, and define the future of live event commerce, we would love to build with you.

 Build AI-first consumer product experiences 
 Invent and ship new ways for fans to discover and buy tickets using AI-powered product thinking and tooling.
 Prototype quickly, validate ideas with data, and iterate into polished experiences that feel simple and delightful.
 Integrate AI into how we build

 Apply AI to analysis and iteration—summarizing qualitative feedback, spotting patterns in product behavior, and turning insights into concrete improvements.
 Deliver features at global scale 
 Build and evolve high-traffic web and mobile product surfaces used by millions of fans.
 Contribute to systems and APIs that support personalization, localization, experimentation, and reliable performance across regions.
 Learn fast with strong mentorship 
 Work closely with experienced engineers who care about clarity, craftsmanship, and setting you up to own features end-to-end.
 What We're Looking for: 
 Recent graduate or software engineer with up to ~1 year of experience (including internships, co-ops, or substantial academic projects).
 Strong CS fundamentals (data structures, algorithms, and core programming concepts).
 Basic experience building user-facing applications and/or consuming APIs.
 Exposure to LLMs or GenAI tools (coursework, internships, hackathons, or side projects)—bonus if you’ve used frameworks or platforms like Anthropic or ChatGPT in something you built.
 Why you’ll love this team: 
 Product impact: You’ll ship directly to fans and see your work in the core StubHub experience.
 AI-first culture: We don’t treat AI as a demo—we use it to build better products and to build faster, across ideation, analysis, implementation, and iteration.
 Experimentation mindset: We run tight loops: build → measure → learn → improve.
 Cross-functional collaboration: Engineers partner deeply with product, design, and data to build experiences that are both effective and enjoyable.
 What We Offer: 
 Accelerated Growth Environment : An environment designed for swift skill and knowledge enhancement, where you have the autonomy to lead experiments and tests on a massive scale.
 Top Tier Compensation Package : Competitive base, equity, and upside that tracks with your impact.
 Flexible Time Of f: Enjoy unlimited Flex Time Off, giving you the flexibility to manage your schedule and take time to recharge as needed.
 Comprehensive Benefits Package : Prioritize your well-being with a comprehensive benefits package, featuring 401k, and premium Health, Vision, and Dental Insurance options.

Base annual salary is one component of StubHub’s total compensation and competitive benefits package, which includes equity, 401(k), paid time off, paid parental leave, and comprehensive health benefits.

 StubHub is the world’s leading marketplace to buy and sell tickets to any live event, anywhere. Through StubHub in North America and viagogo, our international platform, we service customers in 195 countries in 33 languages and 49 available currencies. With more than 300 million tickets available annually on our platform to events around the world -- from sports to music, comedy to dance, festivals to theater -- StubHub offers the safest, most convenient way to buy or sell tickets to the most memorable live experiences. title: Software Engineer I, Marketplace Makers
description:
Company Description 
Etsy is the global marketplace for unique and creative goods. We build, power, and evolve the tools and technologies that connect millions of entrepreneurs with millions of buyers around the world. As an Etsy employee, you will tackle unique, meaningful, and large-scale problems alongside passionate coworkers, all the while making a rewarding impact and Keeping Commerce Human.
 We believe exceptional companies are built by exceptional teams, and we're intentional about it. That means hiring great people, setting them up for success from day one, and giving them real reasons to grow their careers here. We invest in development that goes beyond promotions, and we foster the trust and relationships that help people do their best work together.
 What’s the Role? 
 Etsy is looking for a Software Engineer I to join the Marketplace Makers team. Marketplace Makers are the sellers who create the best buyer experiences on Etsy, and our team builds the programs and tools that recognize and grow them. We work across experiences such as the Star Seller program as well as seller tooling in Shop Manager.
 As a Software Engineer I, you will build and ship full-stack web features in PHP and React/TypeScript, learn how Etsy's platform works end to end, and grow your craft with support from a team that pairs, reviews, and teaches. This is an early-career role: we are looking for someone with a solid programming foundation who is eager to learn how production software is built at scale.
 This is a full time role reporting to the Engineering Manager of Marketplace Makers.
 What’s this team like at Etsy? 
 ● We are a multi-functional product team distributed across the US and Mexico. The team is composed of software engineers, a product manager, a product designer, a researcher, an analyst, and a copywriter.
 ● We work on problems that directly affect millions of sellers: how they earn and keep Star Seller status, and how we motivate the practices, like fast responses and on-time shipping, that create great buyer experiences.
 ● We ship in small increments behind feature flags, run A/B experiments to validate changes, and use data to decide what to build next.
 ● At Etsy, we believe that code is craft and that small, empowered, self-motivated teams can do big things. We take advantage of our continuous deployment system and cultivate a blameless culture based on trust and a commitment to learning. Learn more on our engineering blog: Code as Craft .
 What does the day-to-day look like? 
 ● Build and maintain well-scoped product features across our PHP backend and React/TypeScript frontend, with guidance from senior engineers.
 ● Translate designs and product requirements into production-ready code, and write tests that keep it working.
 ● Participate in code review, both giving and receiving feedback.
 ● Help instrument and analyze A/B experiments on seller-facing features such as the Star Seller dashboard and seller inbox.
 ● Investigate bugs and support issues, and communicate clearly about what you find and how you fixed it.
 ● Collaborate with product, design, research, and analytics partners in planning, standups, and retrospectives.
 ● Of course, this is just a sample of the kinds of work this role will require! You should assume that your role will encompass other tasks, too, and that your job duties and responsibilities may change from time to time at Etsy's discretion, or otherwise applicable with local law.
 Qualities that will help you thrive in this role are: 
 ● A foundation in software engineering, from a degree in computer science or a related field, a bootcamp, or equivalent self-directed experience.
 ● Some experience building web applications, through internships, co-ops, personal projects, or professional work, in languages such as PHP, Python, Ruby, Java, Go, or JavaScript/TypeScript.
 ● Curiosity about how things work and the persistence to debug until you understand the root cause.
 ● Comfort asking questions, taking feedback, and learning in the open.
 ● An interest in solving user problems and in writing code that is readable and maintainable.
 ● Clear written and spoken communication with both technical and non-technical teammates.
 Compensation & Benefits 
 In addition to salary, you'll be eligible for an equity package, an annual performance bonus, and our competitive benefits that support you and your family. Base salary is determined by your location, skills, and experience.
 Etsy uses two geographic pay zones to reflect the labor markets where we compete for talent: one called Geo-1, covering the New York City metropolitan area, San Francisco Bay Area, and Seattle metropolitan area, and one called Geo-2, covering all other U.S. locations. Salary ranges for this role vary by zone and are listed below.
 Location 
 We prioritize candidates based within commutable distance of Etsy’s Brooklyn Office. Depending on proximity, we ask team members to come in once or twice per week. Remote candidates outside commutable distance may be considered on a case-by-case basis, with the expectation of occasional travel to the office. Learn more details about our work modes and workplace safety policies here .
 Salary Range: 
• Geo-1: 120,000.00 - 162,000.00 USD Annual
• Geo-2: 108,000.00 - 146,000.00 USD Annual
 What's Next 
 If you're interested in joining the team at Etsy, please share your resume with us and feel free to include a cover letter if you'd like. As we hope you've seen already, Etsy is a place that values individuality and variety. We don't want you to be like everyone else -- we want you to be like you! So tell us what you're all about.
 Our Promise 
 At Etsy, we believe that a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace furthers relevance, resilience, and longevity. We encourage people from all backgrounds, ages, abilities, and experiences to apply. Etsy is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ethnicity, ancestry, national origin, religion or creed, sex, pregnancy (including childbirth and related medical conditions), gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, citizenship or immigration status, marital or familial status, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status**, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law**. If, due to a disability, you need an accommodation during any part of the interview or hiring process, please let your recruiter know and we will work with you to meet your needs. While Etsy supports visa sponsorship, sponsorship opportunities may be limited to certain roles and skills.

description:
Manufacturing Software Engineer Intern - Winter 2027 | Skydio
San Mateo, California, United States - Intern

Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors to first responders, soldiers in battlefield scenarios, and beyond.

About the role:
At Skydio, we're dedicated to building intelligent flying robots, combining innovative design with cutting-edge technology. Our mission is to make the world more productive, creative, and safe with autonomous flight. We have a deep belief in the transformative power of drones, and our enterprise focus is already making an impact in a wide range of industries across the world.

What makes Skydio different?
- Our drones have the best path-planning and obstacle avoidance thanks to over a decade of R&D in advanced autonomy algorithms.
- We build all parts of the software stack in-house, including embedded systems, middleware, autonomy, cloud infrastructure, manufacturing infrastructure, and automation.
- We design our own hardware to be tightly integrated with our software for maximum performance per gram / per watt.
- We are a U.S. company and manufacture our drones at our factory in California.

As an intern on the Manufacturing Software team, you'll be a core contributor, helping us manufacture high-quality drones, docks and accessories at scale to meet growing customer demands, turning prototypes into finished products. The processes and tools you build will have a significant impact on the company's scale and success.

This team is highly cross-functional. It sits at the intersection of backend (Python + Flask), embedded software (C++/C), frontend (React + Typescript), and electrical engineering (Robotics and Hardware Fixtures).

If you have strong coding fundamentals, thrive on solving and debugging cross-functional challenges, and are passionate about hardware-software systems, this could be a uniquely rewarding opportunity for learning and professional growth.

Our tech:
- Python + Flask backend + on-machine, Protobufs for IPC and RPC
- React + Typescript frontend
- On-premises containerized Linux client machines and servers, AWS backend cloud
- Hardware-in-the-Loop validation systems
- In-house framework for manufacturing and testing operations

Team Project Examples:
- Build and maintain a Hardware-in-the-Loop system for continuous testing of the hardware and software components of our drones and build systems.
- Design a deployment system for sending code physical machines all over the globe, inside of challenging and hostile networks, with redundant safety systems.
- Build a visual configuration tool for documenting and changing how mass production processes work and change on the fly.
- Develop our robot calibration process that can distinguish between hardware and software failures and suggest next steps for assembly rework.
- Create a dashboard that visualizes the state of the factory to help engineers debug faster.
- Develop an automated test fixture that assesses sensors and actuators to minimize operator interaction.

How you'll make an impact:
- Develop an AI-powered triage system that can inspect drone hardware and suggest which parts need to be repaired. Build a framework that combines LLM agents with our manufacturing API in a loop to test the hardware, and compare results against a growing library of root cause failures and suggested reworks.

What makes you a good fit:
- You love having fun building great products and enjoy working on systems that involve both hardware and software
- You are very comfortable with Python and have strong coding fundamentals.
- You're a patient troubleshooter, comfortable asking for help when you need it, and giving help whenever you can.
- You get excited by How It's Made or Factorio and want to get paid to work on the machine that builds the machines.

Compensation Range: The hourly pay for this position is $47/hr*. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. In addition to base salary, Skydio full-time employees are eligible to enroll in our benefit plans and take advantage of a variety of incentives and stipends.
*For some positions the pay may be dependent upon the individual's regional location.

Note: posting title explicitly states Winter 2027; application form asks availability to start January 2027 or February 2027.

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or other characteristics protected by federal, state or local anti-discrimination laws.

For positions located in the United States of America, Skydio, Inc. uses E-Verify to confirm employment eligibility.
